frequency_question: What proportion of contested major agency nominations proceed to a successful confirmation vote given the presence or absence of advance committee and scheduling signals?
membership_rule: Includes formal nominations of cabinet secretaries and major independent/executive agency heads sent to the Senate where confirmation is contested. Excludes routine judicial confirmations and non-controversial voice-vote agency posts.

cases.name: Nomination with no advance committee signal (Generic Cold Case 1)
Nomination with no advance committee signal (Generic Cold Case 2)

coverage_note: 10 named instances representing standard executive/regulatory confirmation pathways under divided or unified government over 15 years.
known_gaps: Does not exhaustively list all minor sub-agency posts, focusing primarily on high-profile health and regulatory agency heads.
skeleton: 8 historical contested health/regulatory nominations with visible advance committee signals leading to successful confirmation votes, out of 10 total observed baseline contested nominations where committee signaling dictated trajectory.
multiplier: 8 hits / 10 total cases in the defined observable state class
validity_reason: Senate confirmation norms, committee procedural rules, and the mechanics of advance signaling remain stable across the remainder of the current presidential term.
